title: Desk bridge v0: brain
description: Talk to the brain through the core: the core holds the session, its lease and the brain client, and streams the answer back as brain.turn events. The core also reads the brain's agent directory (agents, A2A cards, spaces and A2A tasks, specs/brain/v0) and says whether the brain can be reached. Scoped by brain:converse; brain.ask, one question answered through a tool in a session of its own, by brain:ask.

BrainSayRequest.description: Say something to the brain in the desk's current session.

BrainDesk.description: What the person sees as they say the line, as the runtime's window manager holds it (ADR 0109, ADR 0124): the screen and every window, those of the desktop in front first (front to back), then those put away in the drawer, then those of the other desktops in their order; the desktops, the current one marked; the windows closed recently; and a summary of what the person can do. The core puts it before the line, with each plugin's tools, so the brain knows which plugin a request is for, and keeps those words within a fixed size. The desk command desk.windows.list answers the same snapshot, to an agent in the middle of a turn and to the app's tests, which read windows through it rather than through the page (#82).

desktops.description: The desktops (window views, ADR 0117) in their order; `current` marks the one in front. Absent from a runtime before ADR 0124: every window that is not hidden is on the screen.

closed.description: The windows closed recently, the last one closed first; desk.windows.reopen brings one back where it was.

BrainDeskDesktop.description: One desktop (window view): its id, which windows name in `desktop`, its name for people, whether it is the one in front, and how far its canvas is panned.

pan.description: Where its canvas's origin is on screen, in CSS pixels: a normal window on it is drawn this far from its place on the canvas (#82). Absent from a runtime before #82.

BrainDeskOffset.description: An offset in whole CSS pixels.

BrainDeskSize.description: The desk's size in CSS pixels.

BrainDeskWindow.description: One window: where the person sees it in CSS pixels from the desk's top left, each number rounded to the nearest whole pixel, halves up (a window off screen has a rect outside the screen; one on another desktop, where it is when that desktop is in front), its place in its desktop's stacking order, how it is placed (state, and the part of the app a snapped or filled one takes), whether it floats above the canvas, whether it is pinned, whether it has the focus, whether it is put away in the drawer (its rect is where it comes back), the desktop it is on, and its panes.

z.description: Its place in the stacking order of its desktop, from 0 at the back: a window with a higher z is drawn above one with a lower z (floating windows above the normal ones; within each, the window in use on top and pinned ones above the rest). Absent for a window in the drawer, and from a runtime before #82.

pinned.description: Pinned from its title bar: drawn above the windows of its kind that are not, below the one in use.

desktop.description: The id of the desktop it is on (BrainDeskDesktop); absent for a window in the drawer, and from a runtime before ADR 0124.

BrainDeskWindowState.description: How a window is placed (#82): normal, on its desktop's canvas, moving with the canvas's pan; floating, above the canvas, staying where it is on screen while the canvas moves; snapped, taking a half or a quarter of the app (ADR 0128, `fill` names which); filled, taking the whole app (ADR 0132, `fill` is `full`). A snapped or filled window floats too. Absent from a runtime before #82.

BrainDeskFill.description: The part of the app a snapped or filled window takes: the whole app, an edge's half or a corner's quarter (ADR 0128, ADR 0132). Absent for a window that is neither.

BrainDeskPane.description: A pane of a window: its id in the window, the view it shows (plugin:<id>, launcher, an item view), the plugin that draws it, its title for people, whether it is the pane in use, whether that plugin's frame sleeps, and whether it stopped answering the desk.

id.description: The pane's id in its window (p1, p2, ...). Absent from a runtime before #82.

asleep.description: Its plugin's frame sleeps (the live budget, ADR 0070, ADR 0134): the window shows a placeholder and the plugin's last desk:state waits for it until it is in sight or in use again. Absent while the frame is live, and for a frame that was stopped (responsiveness).

BrainDeskResponsiveness.description: How a pane's plugin frame answers the desk (#39), absent while it answers: late, it has not answered for 5 seconds and its window shows Not responding with Wait and Stop (desk.frames.wait, desk.frames.stop); stopped, it was stopped and its window offers Reload (desk.frames.reload).

BrainDeskClosed.description: A window closed recently (ADR 0124): its id, the plugin and title of what it showed, where it was in CSS pixels as for a window on its desktop, whether it floated, the desktop it was on (absent: it was in the drawer, or that desktop is gone) and when it closed.

closedAt.description: When it closed, RFC 3339 on the desk's clock.

BrainDeskCapabilities.description: What the person can do, in short (ADR 0124): how many commands the desk knows (registered, contributed by a plugin that is on, or bound to a key), how many of them can run now and how many have a key, and the plugins that are on. desk.capabilities lists every command with its title, owner, keys and whether it is available.

BrainDeskPlugin.description: A plugin that is on: its title for people, how many of the desk's commands it provides and how many of those can run now, whether its window is on the desk, and the views it opens.

BrainSayResult.description: Result of brain.say: the answer arrives as brain.turn events with this id.

BrainAskRequest.description: Ask the brain one question and get the answer as structured values: the arguments it calls the caller's tool with.

BrainAskParams.description: Parameters of brain.ask: what to ask and the tool whose arguments are the answer.

prompt.description: The question, with everything the brain needs to answer it. The desk's conversation is not sent.

BrainAskTool.description: The tool the brain must call to answer, a ToolDefinition of specs/brain/v0. The core never runs it: the arguments go back to the caller.

name.description: The tool's name, for example propose_theme.

description.description: What the tool is for and when to call it, for the brain.

schema.description: A JSON Schema 2020-12 of the arguments. Its type is object; it may $ref the desk's own specs by their $id.

BrainAskResult.description: Result of brain.ask: the answer arrives as brain.turn events with this id, for the caller only.

BrainAgentsListRequest.description: List the person's agents one page at a time, as the brain's listAgents does.

BrainAgentsListParams.description: Parameters of brain.agents.list: the query of listAgents (specs/brain/v0). A field left out takes the brain's default.

status.description: Only agents with this status, an AgentStatus of specs/brain/v0.

page.description: The page to read, from 1 (the brain's default is 1).

limit.description: Items per page, 1 to 100 (the brain's default is 20).

BrainAgentsListResult.description: Result of brain.agents.list: the brain's AgentList (specs/brain/v0), items newest first and pagination, passed through unchanged.

BrainAgentsCardRequest.description: Read one agent's A2A card, as the brain's getAgentCard does.

agentId.description: The agent's id, as brain.agents.list lists it.

BrainAgentsCardResult.description: Result of brain.agents.card: the brain's AgentCard (specs/brain/v0), passed through unchanged.

BrainSpacesListRequest.description: List the spaces the person can open, as the brain's listSpaces does.

BrainSpacesListResult.description: Result of brain.spaces.list: the brain's SpaceList (specs/brain/v0), passed through unchanged.

BrainTasksListRequest.description: List the A2A tasks agents handed each other one page at a time, as the brain's listA2ATasks does.

BrainTasksListParams.description: Parameters of brain.tasks.list: the query of listA2ATasks (specs/brain/v0). A field left out takes the brain's default.

targetAgentId.description: Only tasks this agent is doing.

status.description: Only tasks with this status, an A2ATaskStatus of specs/brain/v0.

page.description: The page to read, from 1 (the brain's default is 1).

limit.description: Items per page, 1 to 100 (the brain's default is 20).

BrainTasksListResult.description: Result of brain.tasks.list: the brain's A2ATaskList (specs/brain/v0), items newest first and pagination, passed through unchanged.

BrainStatusRequest.description: Which brain the desk talks to, and whether it can be reached now.

BrainStatusResult.description: Result of brain.status: a brain on this machine with its model, a brain in the cloud, or offline.

BrainName.description: A brain the desk can choose for Eris (ADR 0094): endue (endue AI), local (Ollama on this machine), echo (examples/brain-echo) or claude (the person's own Claude Code, asked without its tools, ADR 0109).

BrainStatusLocal.description: A brain on this machine, named by the model it runs. fallback is true when it answers in place of the chosen brain, which cannot be reached now (ADR 0094).

brain.description: The brain the desk chose. Absent from desks that cannot choose.

BrainStatusCloud.description: A brain over the network, such as endue AI. credits is left out while the brain reports none.

brain.description: The brain the desk chose. Absent from desks that cannot choose.

BrainStatusOffline.description: The brain cannot be reached now, or the desk has none.

brain.description: The brain the desk chose, which cannot be reached now. Absent from desks that cannot choose.

BrainTurnEvent.description: Progress of a brain.say or brain.ask turn.

BrainTurnData.description: Payload of brain.turn. delta carries answer text; error and offline carry a sentence for people. A brain.ask turn's completed carries structured when the brain called the tool. tool and tool-result carry tool: a brain.say turn's hand-off to a plugin command and its return (ADR 0089).

structured.description: brain.ask only, on completed: the arguments the brain called the tool with, checked against its schema. Absent when the brain answered in text instead.

BrainTurnKind.description: started, delta (more text), completed; error (the turn failed, for example read-only after a takeover); offline (the brain is unreachable, the turn waits) and online (it resumed); tool (Eris hands work to a plugin command: the core runs the brain's call) and tool-result (the command answered and its answer went back to the brain).

BrainTurnTool.description: tool and tool-result only: the command a brain.say turn's tool call runs, so the desk can show Eris going to its plugin and coming back (ADR 0089).

callId.description: The brain's tool call id; a tool-result names the call it ends.

provider.description: Who provides the command: a plugin id, or desk for the runtime's own.

ok.description: tool-result only: whether the command answered without an error.
